en: The *Tathāgata-siṃhanāda-sūtra*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhayaśas of India during the Northern Wei Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavān was dwelling in the Palace of the Sun and Moon, in the Hall of Supreme Treasure.
The Buddha was together with a great assembly of ninety-nine thousand billion bhikṣus, and eighty-four thousand billion nayutas of hundreds of thousands of koṭis of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Saṃbhavasañcaya, saying:

"Go to the northern direction, past as many Buddha-worlds as there are grains of sand in six thousand koṭis of Ganges Rivers; furthermore, beyond worlds numbering in the hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of calculations, there is a Buddha-world named Joyful."
In that world-system there is a Buddha named Dharmottara Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently lives, remains, and dwells there, preaching the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings.
That Buddha, the World-Honored One, now wishes to proclaim the Vaipulya Dharma-door of the Great Lion’s Roar; you should go and listen to it.
Good son! That supreme Dharma-door is extremely difficult to hear.
The Bodhisattva Jayagarbha accepted the Buddha’s instruction and, practicing according to what was taught, departed for that world.
Having prostrated at the feet of the Tathāgata Dharmodgata and circumambulated him seven times to the right, he withdrew to sit on one side.
Once the Bodhisattva Jayaghoṣa was seated to one side, the Tathāgata Dharmodgata, knowing [his thoughts], asked him:
"Son of good family, from where have you come?
The Bodhisattva Jayaghoṣa remained silent and did not answer.
At that time, the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others in that assembly all had this thought:
"For what reason does this Bodhisattva Sañcaya, the great general of the triple world, remain silent after having been questioned, without providing an answer?"

At that time, the World-Honored One, whose eyes were shaped like broad and long blue lotuses, performed the lion’s sport and surveyed the ten directions. Knowing that the great assembly harbored doubts, he immediately emitted a radiance.

Because he emitted radiance, the Tathāgata Dharmottara sent forth golden light that illuminated the ten directions with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of various colors; at that time, this world shook in six ways.

There were bodhisattvas from the worlds of the ten directions who had gathered in that world, manifesting various physical forms and diverse wondrous appearances; having witnessed the various phenomena of the light rays emitted by that Tathāgata, they assembled in that land and together prostrated at the feet of that Tathāgata.
Having prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, each sat upon a lotus throne according to their own share of roots of goodness and merit.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Vidyut-jvāla rose from his seat, adjusted his robe to bare his left shoulder, approached the Buddha, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and with great joy and exultation, addressed him, saying:
“World-Honored One!
As I now behold the immeasurable radiance emitted by the World-Honored One, I have never before seen such a great light since time immemorial.
Excellent, World-Honored One!
I pray that you will explain this matter.
For what reason does Great Compassion emit this radiance?
I pray that you will explain its significance.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vidyutprabha asked in verse:
“O Great Beings, Supreme among all, This radiance you emit is not without cause or condition;
We pray that you will explain it for our sake.”
"To speak the truth is out of compassion; for the benefit of sentient beings, you emit great rays of light. By what causes and conditions do you speak thus?

At that time, the Bodhisattva Vidyutprabha saw that the body of the Tathāgata was the color of Jambūnada gold, and the immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of rays of light it emitted appeared with sovereign brilliance, like golden banners.
Having seen this, he immediately questioned the Tathāgata Dharmodgata, saying:
"World-Honored One!
I have also previously seen immeasurable lights, but never before have I seen such magnificent and wondrous phenomena as these lights."
That Buddha replied:
"So it is, Vidyutprabhā!
It is just as you have said."
There is a small portion of ground, and upon that ground the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, emit such light; these signs do not appear without cause or condition.
Now, O Vidyutprabhā!
Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon this well; I shall explain for you the matter of how the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, emit rays of light for a specific purpose.
Noble son!
Once you have heard this, do not give rise to alarm or doubt; do not give rise to fear.
Why is this? The realm of all Buddhas is inconceivable; their immeasurable, supreme vows are inconceivable; and the matters of their adornments are inconceivable.
"Good son!
When you see this matter, do not give rise to alarm or doubt.
Diannian, you should know: [the following...]"
"Bodhisattva Jayagarbha was sent to my world, Abhirati, by Śākyamuni Buddha; did you see him?
The Bodhisattva Vidyutprabha replied to that Buddha, "I have seen him."
World-Honored One!
I have seen it. Sugata!
The Buddha said,
“Good son! Regarding this Bodhisattva Sañcaya, I have already asked him:”
"Good man! From where have you come?
He did not answer, but remained silent.
"Good son! It is because I have seen this matter that I emit this radiance. Good son!"
"For what reason did I not answer your question?
Having heard this, the great assembly was struck with alarm and doubt, and remained silent.
The Buddha said:
“Good son! Why is it that this son of good family does not answer when the Tathāgata questions him?
Bodhisattva Śrīsaṃcaya addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Why does the World-Honored One question me regarding the nature of all dharmas in future ages, saying:
‘Good son!’”
"From where have you come? [I replied:
"The Dharma realized by the Buddha is ineffable; the nature of all phenomena is entirely ineffable. I possess no eloquence with which to say that I have come from some particular place."
At that time, the Tathāgata addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O sons of good family!
This son of good family has briefly explained all dharmas and revealed the locus of the true path."

This Bodhisattva Jayamati dwells within the peerless Dharma—which is ineffable and inexpressible, free from letters, transcending high and low, transcending coming and going; where all paths are severed and it is invisible, the state of non-abiding (anālaya); free from mind, intellect, and consciousness; free from the sphere of causes and conditions; nameless and wordless; inexpressible, unspeakable, and unseen; transcending the path of all eyes; not a place of accumulation, not a place of verbal discourse, and not a place that has ever existed; free from the characteristics of signs and even the single letter—namely, that a letter cannot be expressed. How, then, can he answer me?
At that time, the Bodhisattva Prabhāsa, through the Buddha’s spiritual power, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If there is nothing that can be spoken among all dharmas yet there is one who speaks, then all the speech of every deluded person would likewise be the teaching of the Dharma.”
The Buddha said, “Good son!
What has been spoken is not only the teaching of those who are deluded; even those who are not deluded also have teachings, yet though they speak thus, they do not realize it.”
At that time, the Bodhisattva Prabhāsa addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
We pray that the World-Honored One will explain: why is it that all sentient beings preach the Dharma yet do not realize it?”
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Prabhāsa-garbha, saying: "Good son!

It is like a person born blind in this world who, though dwelling by the light of the sun when it shines upon him, cannot know what the appearance of the solar disc is, nor what the color of the sunlight is."
If another person were to say to a blind man,
"The radiance of the sun has such-and-such characteristics," that solar radiance transcends all names and cannot be described by sentient beings.
Due to the occurrence of causes and conditions, one hears these sounds. "Good son!
It is like the various echoes found within deep mountain valleys in the world, which arise due to causes and conditions."
"Good son! The mountain valleys are empty and the echoes are empty; they arise due to causes and conditions. Good son!"

The speech of sentient beings is entirely contained within these analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*): when [the mind] has not yet spoken and the thought has not yet arisen, it is called the analytical knowledge of phenomena (*dharma-pratisaṃvid*);
when the thought has already arisen but speech has not yet been uttered, it is called the analytical knowledge of meaning (*artha-pratisaṃvid*);
and when one reaches the point of expounding by refuting [opposing] doctrines, it is called the analytical knowledge of expression (*nirukti-pratisaṃvid*).
If one speaks with unobstructed and unhindered eloquence, it is called the analytical power of ready speech (*pratibhāna*).
Therefore, son of good family,
all the verbal expressions of all sentient beings do not depart from the meaning of these four dharma-gates, nor do they depart from the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*).
Just as one born blind, when instructed, comes to know the solar orb and its radiance and abandons that conceit,
so too, O son of good family,
those who seek the ultimate meaning should seek it within their own bodies.
“Good son!
Those who wish to seek Bodhi should seek it within the five aggregates (skandhas) of their own bodies.

When this Dharma of the meaning of true words was spoken, that trichiliocosm shook in six ways; a great radiance shone everywhere throughout the world, and the Tathāgata Dharmottara extended his broad and long tongue, covering the entire trichiliocosm.

From within those lights, there further emanated immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of rays of light; these lights illuminated the hells, the hungry ghosts, and the animals, extending upward as far as the Peak of Existence, pervading them all completely.
At that time, that Buddha withdrew his radiance and addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O sons of good family!
There is never such a case where a tongue-mark and its radiance exist yet one speaks falsely; you should all have faith and mindfulness, for what I say is the truth."

At that time, the Bodhisattvas dwelling on the tenth stage stood as the leaders of the assembly. All those in the assembly—devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans—rose from their seats, joined their palms, and with one voice spoke these words:

“We pray that the World-Honored One will speak; we pray that the Sugata will explain the meaning of the Dharma as it truly is. By the spiritual power of the Buddha, this great assembly shall never harbor any doubt.”
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the great assembly, saying:
“O sons of good family!
This is a great lion’s roar which I now wish to proclaim, for the sake of bringing peace, happiness, and benefit to all sentient beings, and even to devas and humans.”
"Good son!

In that Sahā world there is a World-Honored One, titled Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who at this very moment is living, existing, and abiding, preaching the Dharma for the sake of the assembly."
"Good son! It is I myself who am now present here.
For the sake of benefiting sentient beings, the Tathāgata Dharmottara manifested various forms in that Sahā world and preached the Dharma for them."
At that time, having heard these words, the great assembly was filled with immense joy and leaped for joy beyond measure, exclaiming to the Tathāgata:
“Excellent, excellent!”
World-Honored One!
May all sentient beings likewise utter such a great lion’s roar, just as the World-Honored One now utters a great lion’s roar within this assembly.
World-Honored One!
If there are those who hear this lion’s roar, those sentient beings cannot be said to have planted even a small root of goodness.

How much more so for those who, having heard the Tathāgata’s great lion’s roar, believe and accept it; and how much more so for those who further read, recite, receive, uphold, extensively explain it to others, and make offerings to this sutra with incense, flowers, unguents, powdered incense, burning incense, various garments, precious banners, and precious canopies?
World-Honored One, you should know that these sentient beings are empowered by the Buddha.
If there are those who hear even a single phrase of this sutra of the Great Lion’s Roar pass through their ears, those sentient beings have not planted merely minor roots of goodness or merit.
At that time, the World-Honored One praised that bodhisattva, saying these words:
“Excellent, excellent!
O son of good family!”
As you have said:
those sentient beings did not plant even a small amount of roots of goodness or merit to be able to hear this.

If they can hear these words of the sūtra spoken by the Tathāgata as a great lion’s roar, and give rise to a heart of joy, even uttering a single word of praise, saying "Excellent!"—O son of good family!
These are protected by me and protected by the Bodhisattva Maitreya; they all bear my enlightenment upon their shoulders.

If, within this world of five turbidities, one is able to believe and accept this sutra, such a person was already transformed by me in the past and is also protected by the Bodhisattva Ajita. That person has already exhausted the great ocean of birth and death; has already subdued the hosts of Māras and eliminated afflictions; has already thundered the Dharma-thunder and struck the Dharma-drum; has already abandoned the female body; has already conquered all enemies; and has already been able to extinguish the multitude of all afflictions.

“Good son! If there were good sons or good daughters who, with all manner of requisites for making offerings, were to provide offerings to as many Tathāgatas as would fill ten *asaṃkhyeya* trichiliocosms;

yet if another were to hear a single phrase of this *sūtra* on the True Meaning and be able to believe and accept it, and because of that faith exclaim ‘Excellent!’—the merit obtained by the latter would surpass that of the former’s offering to the Tathāgatas of the trichiliocosm.”
For this reason, sons of good family!
If you have faith in my words, you should write down and uphold this sutra.
Sons of good family!
"In whatever place this sutra is written down and honored, one should know that the Tathāgata is present in that household.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Jayaghoṣa, the Bodhisattva Vidyutprabha, the Bodhisattva Nityaprabha, the Bodhisattva Viśuddhacakṣus, the Bodhisattva Abhayadatta, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, the Bodhisattva Pratibhānasaṃcaya, the Bodhisattva Sarvāvaraṇavikiraṇa, the Bodhisattva Prabhākara, and the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra—these eighty-four trillion hundred thousand bodhisattvas addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
"In future ages, we shall widely proclaim these phrases of this Dharma-gate.
World-Honored One!
Those sentient beings who hear this sutra are also said to have attained nirvana."
"Bhagavān!
If there are sentient beings who are able to believe in this sūtra, those beings have not merely planted a small amount of roots of goodness for the first time.
Bhagavān!"

If even hearing this sutra once passes through one's ears, how much more so for those who fully master, read, recite, and uphold it? The merit obtained by such sentient beings could not be exhausted even if explained for hundreds of thousands of billions of kalpas.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!
O sons of good family!"
"You all should thus protect and uphold the True Dharma of the Tathāgata.
When the Buddha spoke this Dharma-gate, the Bodhisattva Jayaghoṣa and the entire great assembly were all filled with great joy.
The Tathāgata-Siṃhanāda Sūtra
